entries.claim: The pinned Latin Mass data independently corroborate the component's substantive Latin and expose accidental editorial variants for collation.

locator.section: RG 115 a; conclusion and textual Amen w025–w047

entries.claim: RG 115 a in the Benziger printing supplies the full Father-directed conclusion and textual Amen for w025–w047. The initial mention of the Son requires the separately cited RG 115 b eundem variant. The witness declares house accents, ligatures, tuum: Qui and final Amen. in place of the rubric typography; this is an expansion, not complete diplomatic wording on the proper page.

The Benziger printing on p. 336 directly prints the 24-word proper body w001–w024 and its abbreviated Per eundem Dominum nostrum cue. The full conclusion and textual Amen w025–w047 are expanded through separately cited general rubrics, not fully printed on this proper page.

locator.section: RG 480–481, 511 d/i, 513–514; Ordo Missae rubric and chant formula after the secrets

entries.claim: The final secret has an audible Per omnia saecula saeculorum followed by the response Amen. Collects and postcommunions are priestly orations with a separate response. These rules determine the modeled boundaries, not the completeness of a date-specific commemoration inventory.

locator.section: RG 115 b; initial mention of the Son and eundem variant

entries.claim: RG 115 b in the Benziger printing prescribes Per eundem Dominum nostrum when a Father-directed prayer mentions the Son at its beginning. Filii tui in this Collect establishes that condition; RG 115 a supplies the remainder and Amen.
